candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is Progressive Ataxia and Palatal Tremor (PAPT), sporadic type — a composite syndrome requiring both progressive cerebellar ataxia and palatal tremor/myoclonus. 'Palatal Myoclonus, spontaneous' addresses only one component (the palatal movement disorder) and omits the defining progressive ataxia element and the sporadic PAPT classification. The clinical record clearly documents both components (20-year progressive ataxia with cerebellar atrophy plus continuous palatal myoclonus), so the candidate is a component/manifestation of the full syndrome rather than the complete diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Palatal myoclonus (spontaneous) captures only the palatal tremor component of PAPT and does not encompass the progressive ataxia syndrome or its sporadic subtype designation

case_quality_flags: Palatal myoclonus in PAPT is now more precisely termed 'palatal tremor' in current nosology; the candidate uses older 'myoclonus' terminology consistent with the case documentation but does not affect the partial equivalence judgment
Sporadic PAPT subtype is clinically supported by negative SCA genetic panel and absence of family history, reinforcing the reference diagnosis specificity
